messages.subject: Global mapping of multiple categories by colour
parts:
Dear All,

I was sent here from the r-sig-geo mailing list,  so I'm sorry if you have seen this before. I have to make a last minute global map. I'm trying to do this in r, but I am a beginner.

I have a global dataset of dependent values (eg. rate of common cold) for 100/240 countries/offshore territories. I have a predictor
variable (eg. Human development index or HDI). What I would like to do is colour a global map by HDI grouping (low [0-0.5], medium[0.51-0.7],
high[0.71-1.0]). So for countries that I have data for, if it is low HDI it would be colour1, medium colour 2, low colour3. For countries with no data they will be a fourth colour (grey), and inland countries white.

Additionally, some small island nations will be too small to be visualized. Is there a way to manually increase the size of the colouration to be visible on a map at the global scale?

Sample data3 is as such (where blanks are no data):

country   hdi
              0
              0
              0
  ASM     0.827
               0
               0
   AGO     0.392
               0
    ATG    0.86
               0
               0
   SHN     0.52

My code so far is as follows:

library(rworldmap)
  data2=read.table("Map4csv.csv",header=T,sep=",")
 country= as.character(data2$alpha3)
  hdi=data2$HDI
  data3<-cbind(country,hdi)
   data3<-data.frame(data3)

malMap <- joinCountryData2Map(dF = data3, joinCode = "ISO3", nameJoinColumn = "country")
# This will join your malDF data.frame to the country map data

mapCountryData(malMap, nameColumnToPlot="hdi", catMethod = "categorical", missingCountryCol = gray(.8))

The country codes match up. Where I am stuck now is how to divide the countries into the three hdi groups mentioned above.
I have tried playing around with different permutations of the "catMethod and "numCats". For example:

mapCountryData(malMap, nameColumnToPlot="hdi", catMethod = "categorical", missingCountryCol = gray(.8), numCats = 3)

Even when I try running this it produces a map where the whole range of numbers are used as categories (attached figure).

So my questions are:
1) How do I set three distinct bins with discrete ranges (red = 0-0.5, yellow = 0.51-.8, green = 0.81-1)
2) How do I make inland countries white?
3) How do I make small island nation's colouring bigger so they are more visible?

(For #3 Andy, you have mentioned to use of mapBubbles([some stuff],add=TRUE). I will try and play around with this once the categories work).

Thank you all in advance.

Cheers,

Sarah

messages.author: 1d1f3e09391145a0
messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Global mapping of multiple categories by colour
parts:
Here's some code from a map that Andy helped me with (described at http://alienplantation.wordpress.com/2013/06/18/nuts-and-bolts-modern-maps-of-eurasia-in-r/ and code at https://gist.github.com/kgturner/5799785). Basically, you add a column to your data, identifying the bin you want it to be colored.

#setup a color code column filled with 1's
sPDF$colCode <- 1

#set codes for specified countries
sPDF$colCode[ which(sPDF$ADMIN %in% c("Canada","United States of America"))] <- 2
sPDF$colCode[ which(sPDF$ADMIN %in% c("Armenia","Azerbaijan", "Bulgaria", "Georgia",
                                      "Greece", "Moldova", "Romania","Russia", "Turkey",
                                      "Ukraine", "Serbia"))] <- 3
sPDF$colCode[ which(sPDF$ADMIN %in% c("Poland", "Belarus", "Italy", "Syria", "Czech Republic",
                                      "Estonia", "Switzerland","Latvia","Lithuania",
                                      "Slovenia", "Serbia","Austria","Belgium", "France",
                                      "Germany","Hungary","Luxembourg","Norway","Slovakia",
                                      "Spain", "United Kingdom", "Kazakhstan", "Turkmenistan", "China"))] <- 4

#create a colour palette - note for each value not for each country
colourPalette <- c("lightgray","#F8766D","#00BFC4", "cadetblue1")

par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
mapCountryData(sPDF, nameColumnToPlot="colCode", mapTitle=NA,
               colourPalette=colourPalette, borderCol ='gray24', addLegend = FALSE,
               xlim=xlim, ylim=ylim, catMethod=c(0,1,2,3,4))
#note that catMethod defines the breaks and values go in a category if they are <= upper end

Hope that helps,
Kathryn Turner

Here's some code that should produce the attached pdf map from your datafile.

data2=read.csv("Map4csv.csv")
op <- palette(c('red','yellow','green'))

malMap <- joinCountryData2Map(dF = data2, joinCode = "ISO3", nameJoinColumn = "alpha3")

mapParams = mapCountryData(  malMap
                           , nameColumnToPlot="HDI"
                           , addLegend=FALSE
                           , colourPalette = op
                           , catMethod=c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 1.1) )


# add a legend        
do.call( addMapLegendBoxes, c(mapParams, title="HDI value"))

Andy
